title: four ways of naming Capability.context without calling it — as an argument, as a parenthesised argument, through a const alias, and through .call — are all refused
notes: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Context Access': '`Capability.context()` MUST be an inherited, compiler-recognized call' whose meaning is to 'add that class's nominal identity to the enclosing function's inferred R row', and 'Lookup MUST remain fully typed. The implementation MUST NOT expose an untyped service locator.' A reference to `context` that is not called is a value the compiler cannot attribute: whoever eventually calls it is not the function that named it, so no row can be recorded and the read becomes exactly the untyped locator the specification forbids. WHY THESE FOUR SPELLINGS: the corpus already refuses `Reflect.apply(Reader.context, ...)` and `Reader.context.bind(Reader)()` in two older cases, both of which name the reference through a well-known reflective member. These four are the shapes that do not: handing it to a local function, handing it to a local function through a parenthesis, binding it to a `const` and calling the const, and `.call`. The parenthesised argument at line 12 is the load-bearing one and the reason this case was written this round — it is one token away from `(Reader.context)()`, which is a legitimate capability read that the Go fork refused as detached until 2026-08-27. The two spellings must get OPPOSITE answers, and no rule that keys on 'a parenthesis appears around `X.context`' can produce that. Lines 11 and 12 are therefore a matched pair with `a-parenthesised-context-callee-is-still-a-context-call`, and the pair is the whole content. WHAT THIS CASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: the message. `SMITHERS2107` carries one fixed sentence, worded identically on both backends, that names the rule and no part of this program — there is no capability name, no spelling, nothing a wrong-but-plausible refusal could get wrong — so `messageContains` would only freeze wording. It also does not pin a `SMITHERS2102`: a detached reference records no row, so there is no unsatisfied requirement to report at the top level, and declaring one would ratify a cascade neither backend produces. It also does not pin `Reflect.apply` or `.bind`, which have their own cases; duplicating them here would make three files break together for one cause. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the declared column on line 12 from 67 to 66 — one column left, onto the parenthesis rather than the member expression, which is precisely where a rule that anchored at the outermost node would report — turns the case red on BOTH backends with the position diff printed, and the file was restored byte-identically (sha256 3f9e83d116e6d3a8b8f71812c32a24bcf318ad5253e578283a6c06725490f799 before and after, that digest being this file's content at the moment the mutation ran — the sentence recording it is appended afterwards, so the shipped file necessarily hashes differently). The paired positive control is `a-parenthesised-context-callee-is-still-a-context-call`, which must keep compiling AND RUNNING.
